profile.home: Anchovies school near the surface in coastal and open waters worldwide.
profile.diet: Most strain plankton from the water and also snap up tiny prey.

profile.superpower: A crowded school makes it hard for a predator to choose one target.

profile.name: Sardine Ball
profile.tagline: A silver swirl that makes predators dizzy.
profile.intro: A sardine ball is a tightly packed school of small, silvery fishes that turns almost like one giant animal. Sardine is a shared name for several members of the herring family, so this SeaPals creature represents the whole group.
profile.home: Sardines gather in plankton-rich coastal and open waters around the world.
profile.diet: They eat tiny plankton, including drifting animals and microscopic algae.
profile.size: Usually 6-12 in (15-30 cm)—about ruler length
profile.superpower: Thousands of neighbors can turn together in an instant and confuse attackers.
funFacts: Each fish follows nearby neighbors rather than a single school leader.
A dark back and pale belly camouflage sardines from above and below.
Sardines are important food for seabirds, marine mammals, and larger fishes.
Their lateral-line sensors detect vibrations and nearby movement in the water.
